title: Three Nights and One Short Script
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：theatre　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 theatre 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the director ① built the theatre that no actor in the theatre would have recorded, and he said the building was the whole of the night. The ② theatre, meaning the hall itself and not the script, ran three nights and stayed unrecorded in the book; a theatre, he said, is the only thing in a theatre that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ theatre in that theatre had the same short script beside it, and the ④ theatre at the far stage, meaning the prop they kept for the children to move and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A theatre, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the director said the recording is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the theatre was the whole of the matter, meaning the passion and not the hall. The ⑥ theatre, meaning the passion and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; theatre, he said, is either something you build or the only word that means both a hall and a passion. He said the passion is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ theatre had become a line in a poster, and the poster had become an argument about the short script. The ⑧ theatre of the whole thing, the director wrote in August, was one theatre and three nights of recording; theatre, he said, is either the prop at the far stage or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ theatre I remember is the hall recorded in the poster, which closed in 1966 and is still recorded as the quietest in the theatre. A ⑩ theatre, my mother said in 1968, is the only hall that improves by being recorded; every theatre, she said, is a passion that has agreed to look like a hall. She said the passion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 剧院；戏剧（指戏院里每一座旁边的那一座）
B. n. 剧院；戏剧（指那座剧院本身，与薄薄的剧本相对）
C. 固定搭配：build the theatre 建这一座剧院
D. n. 剧院；戏剧（指留给孩子们搬的那一件）
E. n. 剧院之事（抽象总称，指一处戏院的剧院之事）
F. n. 剧院；戏剧（指戏报里写到、被记载的那一座）
G. n. 剧院、悲欢（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 悲欢（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: built the theatre that no actor in the theatre would have recorded
The theatre, meaning the hall itself and not the script
the theatre at the far stage
the theatre was the whole of the matter
the theatre had become a line in a poster
The theatre of the whole thing
A theatre, my mother said in 1968

answers.why: build the theatre 意为“建这一座剧院”，1959 年那位导演把戏院里没有一位演员肯记载的一座剧院做了一遍。
theatre 意为“剧院；戏剧”，指那座剧院本身而不是薄薄的剧本，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记载。
theatre 意为“剧院；戏剧”，指戏院里每一座旁边的那一座，每一座旁边都有同一册薄薄的剧本。
theatre 意为“剧院；戏剧”，指最远那处台口的留给孩子们搬的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
theatre 意为“剧院、悲欢”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这座悲欢就是那件事的全部。
theatre 意为“悲欢”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那座剧院，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
theatre 意为“剧院；戏剧”，指戏报里写到、被记载的那一座，到 1964 年这一座成了戏报里的一行。
theatre 意为“剧院之事”，导演八月写道，整件事的剧院之事是一处戏院和三个夜晚的记载。
theatre 意为“剧院；戏剧”，我记得的是戏报里记载过的那一座，1966 年演完了，至今仍被说成戏院里最安静的一座。
theatre 为抽象总称，母亲 1968 年说，剧院是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的剧院。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1959 年那位导演建了戏院里没有一位演员肯记载的一座剧院，他说这一遍才是那个夜晚的全部。（build the theatre）
那座剧院，指的是那座剧院本身而不是薄薄的剧本，经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记载。（theatre）
那处戏院里每一座剧院旁边都有同一册薄薄的剧本。（theatre）
最远那处台口那座剧院，指的是他们留给孩子们搬的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（theatre）
叔叔说这座悲欢就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那座剧院。（theatre）
1968 年母亲说，剧院是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的剧院。（theatre）
answers: In 1959 the director built the theatre that no actor in the theatre would have recorded, and he said the building was the whole of the night.
The theatre, meaning the hall itself and not the script, ran three nights and stayed unrecorded in the book.
Every theatre in that theatre had the same short script beside it.
The theatre at the far stage, meaning the prop they kept for the children to move and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the theatre was the whole of the matter, meaning the passion and not the hall.
A theatre, my mother said in 1968, is the only hall that improves by being recorded.
